title: UPSC CSE - Medieval India - Mughal Empire (1526 AD to 1761 AD)
subject: Medieval India

questions.q: Yogavasistha was translated into Persian by Nizamuddin Panipati during the reign of:
questions.explain: YogaVasistha was translated into Persian multiple times throughout the Mughal Dynasty, as commanded by Akbar, Jahangir, and Darah Shikuh. Nizam al-Din Panipati completed one of these translations, known as the Jug-Basisht, in the late sixteenth century AD.

questions.q:
With reference to medieval India, which one of the following is the correct sequence in ascending order in terms of size?
(a) Paragana—Sarkar—Suba
(b) Sarkar—Paragana—Suba
(c) Suba—Sarkar—Paragana
(d) Paragana—Suba—Sarkar
questions.explain: During the Mughal time, there were large provinces called Suba. Every Suba was divided into several Sarkars or districts. Each Sarkar was divided into smaller units called Parganas. So, the correct order is Paragana - Sarkar – Suba.

questions.q: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to the album and individual portraits?
questions.explain: Akbar's reign saw illustrations of manuscripts, the prominent being Razmnama which is the Persian translation of Mahabharata. It was during Jahangir's reign that manuscripts became less important and there was more focus on individual portraits. Under Jahangir, paintings acquired greater charm, refinement, and dignity.

questions.q: With reference to Mian Tansen, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Tansen was the title given to him by Emperor Akbar.
Tansen composed Dhrupads on Hindu gods and goddesses.
Tansen composed songs for his patrons.
questions.explain: Tansen was a court musician in the darbar of Raja Ram Chandra of Bandavagarh (Rewa). Tansen was the title given to him by Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior. Tansen is also known as the 'Sangit Samrat', according to Musical Heritage of India by Lalita Ramakrishna.

questions.q:
With reference to Mughal India, what is/are the difference/differences between Jagirdar and Zamindar?
1. Jagirdars were holders of land assignments in lieu of judicial and police duties, whereas Zamindars were holders of revenue rights without obligation to perform any duty other than revenue collection.
2. Land assignments to Jagirdars were hereditary and the revenue rights of Zamindars were not hereditary.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Both statements are incorrect. Jagirdars were mansabdars given salary in lieu of military services in terms of jagirs (land). Zamindars were local elite who exercised authority in their areas. Land assignments to Jagirdars were not hereditary, while Zamindars' positions were hereditary.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
The arrival of Babur into India led to the
1. introduction of gunpowder
2. introduction of the arch and dome in the region's architecture
3. establishment of the Timurid dynasty
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Gunpowder was introduced by the Mongols in the 13th century. Arch and dome architecture was prevalent during the Delhi Sultanate. Babur established the Timurid dynasty in India, known as the Mughal Empire.

questions.q: Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was
options: the mosque for the use of the Royal Family
the hall in which Akbar held discussions with scholars of various religions
the room in which the nobles belonging to different religions gathered to discuss religious affairs
questions.explain: Ibadat Khana was constructed by Akbar in 1575. It was initially a place for Muslim scholars to discuss Islam, but later Akbar opened it to scholars of other religions, making it the first attempt at secularism, also known as 'Din-i-Ilahi'.
